newsitem.title: USA: Clinton safeguards fit for a king - Jones attorney.
newsitem.headline: Clinton safeguards fit for a king - Jones attorney.

text.p: An attorney for the woman who filed a sexual harassment lawsuit against President Bill Clinton said on Sunday the argument against allowing the case to proceed was one a monarch would use to safeguard privileges.

The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday is to hear arguments on whether the lawsuit by Paula Jones from Arkansas should be allowed to proceed while Clinton is still in the White House or deferred until he leaves.
"What the president has put forth in this case is a troubling, novel claim of personal privilege," Joseph Cammarata, an attorney for Jones, said on ABC Television's "This Week."

"If you believe the president, then we have a monarchy, we have a king," he said. "If you believe Paula Jones, then we have public servants that remain accountable for their own personal, private conduct."
The Supreme Court will focus on when Jones's lawsuit can go forward, not on the merits of her allegations which Clinton has denied.
Jones seeks $700,000 in damages in the case in which she contended Clinton made unwanted advances in 1991 in a Little Rock hotel room when he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee.

Cammarata called the argument that the lawsuit should not proceed while Clinton was president the "Chicken Little defence" with contentions that "there's going to a parade of horribles, lawsuits will be unleashed and I'll be tied up forever."

Asked why women's groups have not come out in support of Jones, Cammarata replied: "Well, it's very distressing, quite frankly. I think it's the height of hypocrisy on the part of the women's groups."

A recent survey by Time Magazine and CNN showed 56 percent of the people polled said Jones should be allowed to continue her lawsuit while Clinton was still in office, while 39 percent said the lawsuit should be postponed.
